RoomTreasury project intake
Project name: Digital Agency Website — Design and Development
Description: Design and develop a modern, professional and responsive website for NovaCreative Agency, a fictional digital agency offering web development, branding and AI automation services. The website should establish the agency's online presence, showcase its services and portfolio, communicate its working process, and generate enquiries from prospective clients.
Requirements and scope: Build a responsive six-section business website.

HOMEPAGE

Professional hero section with a strong headline.

Supporting description explaining the agency's value proposition.

Primary call-to-action button.

ABOUT

Agency introduction.

Mission, values and approach to client projects.

SERVICES
Four service offerings:

Website Design and Development.

UI/UX Design.

AI Automation Solutions.

Digital Branding.
Each service must have a title and description.

PORTFOLIO

Three fictional project examples.

Each example includes a title, short description and image placeholder.

OUR PROCESS
Display five stages:

Discovery.

Planning.

Design.

Development.

Delivery.

CONTACT

Contact information.

Functional email link.

Clear enquiry call-to-action.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

Responsive desktop, tablet and mobile layouts.

Modern, accessible frontend design.

Functional navigation and section links.

Consistent typography, spacing and visual identity.

Optimized images and reasonable load
Deliverables: DELIVERABLES

Complete responsive six-section website.

Four service cards.

Three portfolio project entries.

Five-stage process section.

Functional navigation and contact email link.

Source code and basic deployment instructions.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
All six sections must be implemented and work correctly on desktop, tablet and mobile. Navigation and contact links must function, and the website must have no major visual or functional defects.
Desired deadline: Not specified
Additional notes: This is a synthetic test project. The $1,800 is a proposed estimate only, not confirmed client revenue, a signed contract, received cash or available delivery funds. No deadline has been agreed. The agency should estimate project effort, resources, delivery timeline, risks and financial exposure. All spending must remain simulated and require human approval. No real client, payment or external commitment exists.

finalReport.reportText:
@make-proposal-agent rt-task-39d913b9-f059-48b7-b3a8-d5f9a6722164-REQ — FINAL REQUIREMENTS SPECIALIST REPORT
Binding: project 804019a2-0012-4f8d-964e-1caa343e82a4 | job e8c2e4a1-1546-45b3-b9f2-80b05000ecca | correlation discord-e8c2e4a1-1546-45b3-b9f2-80b05000ecca | intake revision 1.
Analysis only: no project/financial record, approval, commitment, reservation, settlement, deployment, or agent change occurred.

A. Executive Summary
The authoritative synthetic intake defines one responsive six-section business website, not six separate pages. It has fixed synthetic content requirements—four services, three fictional portfolio examples with image placeholders, and five process stages—plus functional anchors/navigation and a mailto contact link. Source code and basic deployment instructions are required deliverables; public deployment, CMS, form, email notifications, SEO campaign and portfolio detail pages are not requested. Requirements are sufficiently bounded for a conditional synthetic proposal, but acceptance needs a documented test matrix and proposed load limits; no real-client clarification is necessary for fictional placeholder assets.

B. Confirmed Requirements
Evidence: original attachment roomtreasury-intake.txt, downloaded from switch-media://77d910f3c62c44129636e9818d9899de and dispatched in sw_c0b32f8f10bc694ff49ca20d06b285c4; assignment sw_1ef13f1636b945dda4b31cbf03a4460d.
- One responsive six-section site: Home, About, Services, Portfolio, Our Process, Contact.
- Home: professional hero, headline, value proposition/supporting description, primary CTA.
- About: agency introduction, mission, values, approach.
- Services: exactly four titled/described cards: Website Design and Development; UI/UX Design; AI Automation Solutions; Digital Branding.
- Portfolio: exactly three fictional examples, each with title, short description and image placeholder.
- Process: Discovery, Planning, Design, Development, Delivery.
- Contact: contact information, functional email link, clear enquiry CTA.
- Desktop/tablet/mobile layouts; accessible modern frontend; functional navigation/section links; consistent typography, spacing and visual identity; optimized images and reasonable load.
- Deliverables: complete website, four cards, three entries, five-stage process, navigation/mail link, source code, basic deployment instructions.
- Acceptance: all six sections work on desktop/tablet/mobile; navigation/contact links work; no major visual/functional defects.
- No deadline is specified/agreed. 180000 USD cents is a proposed estimate only—not contract, agreed/received revenue, funds or a commitment. The brief states no real client, payment or external commitment exists.

C. Proposed Requirements / Synthetic Defaults
These are bounded interpretations, not client confirmations:
- A single scrolling page with six identifiable section anchors is the recommended implementation. Separate routes/pages are not implied.
- Primary CTA should link to the Contact section; navigation links should target the six section IDs.
- The portfolio’s three image placeholders are complete synthetic scope, not missing production assets. They can use clearly labeled neutral placeholder graphics/blocks; no rights clearance, photography, video or real portfolio content is required.
- Contact email behavior is limited to a visible mailto link using a designated synthetic/configurable address. A mailto URL can be link-tested; sending/receiving email cannot be warranted without a mail client/account and is not in scope.
- No CMS, contact form, email notification service, SEO campaign, project-detail page, analytics, paid service, custom integration or public deployment should be added.

D. Scope and Deliverables
1. Responsive single-page six-section frontend, including fixed section content and visual hierarchy.
2. Four service cards, three synthetic portfolio placeholders, and five named process stages.
3. Functional header/navigation anchors, primary CTA-to-contact behavior, and contact mailto link.
4. Responsive/accessibility and performance QA evidence against agreed/proposed checks.
5. Source-code package with README/basic deployment instructions: prerequisites, install/build command(s), environment/configuration notes if any, local preview, and static-hosting deployment steps. This does not require hosting an application.
Proposed exclusions: live deployment, DNS/hosting procurement, form/notification backend, CMS/editorial tools, real photography/assets, content workflow, SEO campaign/ranking guarantee, ongoing maintenance/support, analytics, project detail pages, and work beyond the stated six sections.

E. Acceptance Criteria
Functional/structure:
- Each of the six named sections is present exactly once and contains its confirmed elements; Services has four titled/described cards, Portfolio has three title/description/placeholder entries, and Process has five named stages.
- Every navigation item and primary CTA resolves to the intended in-page section; no broken fragment links.
- Contact mailto link contains a valid mailto href and can be invoked in browser link testing; outbound email delivery is excluded.
Responsive:
- On one agreed desktop, tablet and mobile viewport, sections remain readable, navigation/CTA/mailto are usable, there is no unintended horizontal overflow, and no element obscures essential content or controls. Exact browser/device matrix is not supplied.
Accessibility smoke checks (not certification):
- Keyboard users can reach navigation, CTA and mailto in a logical order; focus is visibly discernible.
- Interactive elements have accessible names; semantic heading order is sensible; placeholder images are marked decorative or have accurate alternative text as appropriate.
- Text/controls remain distinguishable under the implemented visual design. No WCAG conformance claim is made.
No-major-defect rule:
- Major = a required section missing; a required link/control nonfunctional; core content unreadable/unreachable at tested viewport; or a defect preventing required navigation/contact behavior. Zero major defects in the agreed test matrix.
- Cosmetic discrepancies that do not block a required flow are recorded separately; their acceptance is not pre-authorized.

F. Proposed bounded SEO/performance/load criteria — explicitly unapproved assumptions
The intake requests optimized images/reasonable load but supplies no metric, test tool, device, network or threshold. For a static synthetic review build only, I propose:
- Home/initial route transfer target: ≤3 MB network transfer; each placeholder image target ≤500 KB; record actual measured transfer size rather than claiming compliance without a test.
- Test one agreed desktop profile and one mobile profile using a named browser audit/tool; record date, URL/build, viewport/profile, total transfer size, request count, LCP/CLS where the tool reports them, and limitations. No score, ranking, CWV target, SLA or guaranteed load time is implied.
- Verify page title, one logical primary heading, descriptive link labels and no broken anchors. This is basic technical hygiene, not an SEO campaign or indexing/public-launch commitment.
- Optimize only identified avoidable issues such as oversized placeholder images or unnecessary blocking assets. Because no public deployment is requested, robots/sitemap/canonical/indexation decisions are not acceptance requirements unless later added.

G. Necessary Clarifications vs Synthetic Defaults
Not blocking under the stated synthetic brief:
- Real logo, real copy, real portfolio media, real contact identity/mailbox, rights, payment or real customer approval—explicitly absent/fictional; placeholders are expected scope.
- Public host/DNS, live email delivery, provider selection and ongoing support—none requested.
Blocking only if scope is expanded:
- Whether six sections must become separate pages/routes.
- A real recipient address or demonstrated delivery if the client changes mailto to real enquiry handling.
- CMS/form/notifications, real assets, public launch, SEO/indexing, analytics, browser support matrix, performance targets, accessibility conformance level, deadline or support terms.
- Any future definition of reasonable load different from the proposed bounded test criteria.
These changes are new proposed scope and require re-estimation/review; they are not implicit clarifications missing from this synthetic assignment.

H. Dependencies and Timeline
No deadline/start date is evidenced. Conditional sequence: content/placeholder design → single-page implementation → responsive/accessibility/link/performance checks → source/README handover. Delivery duration can only be estimated by the responsible cost/treasury specialists after assumptions and capacity are established. Basic deployment instructions depend on selected framework/build tool and a static-hosting target example, but do not require credentials or actual deployment.

I. Risks and Concerns
- Medium scope risk: treating sections as pages, adding CMS/form/public launch or real assets creates unstated work. Mitigation: preserve the single-page and synthetic-placeholder boundaries.
- Medium mailto risk: browsers may lack configured mail clients; this is an environment behavior, not a frontend failure. Mitigation: accept correct href invocation, not delivery.
- Medium accessibility risk: accessible is broad without a standard. Mitigation: use listed smoke checks and avoid certification claims.
- Medium performance risk: reasonable load lacks benchmarks. Mitigation: adopt proposed measurable limits only if coordinator/owner chooses them; record rather than invent results.
- Low handover risk: source code without accurate build/deploy notes is incomplete. Mitigation: require tested README instructions against the chosen toolchain.
- Low provenance risk: supplied SHA-256 is intake metadata; canonical hashing inputs are unspecified, so its cryptographic correctness cannot be asserted.

J. Cross-Agent Findings
No current-task findings from challenge, commitment intelligence, or treasury were available to this specialist at report completion. I make no claim about schedule, resource availability, commitments, cost, revenue feasibility or margin. Their actual reports must remain separately attributed.

K. Recommendations
1. Adopt the six-section, one-page synthetic baseline and explicitly retain all stated exclusions.
2. Use the acceptance matrix above, including link/anchor/mailto invocation, three responsive classes, keyboard/focus smoke checks, and zero major defects.
3. Treat the proposed load criteria as optional planning limits pending coordinator/owner adoption; record audit evidence.
4. Require source-code README/deployment instructions as a handover gate, with no claim of public deployment.
5. If requirements change to real assets, mail delivery, CMS/form, public launch or separate pages, create a new scope revision and obtain independent cost/risk/financial review.

L. Final Requirements Decision
READY_WITH_EXPLICIT_ASSUMPTIONS for a synthetic, source-code-and-instructions proposal only. It is NOT ready for a real deployment, client acceptance, financial approval or any inferred expanded scope. Confidence: High for requirements extraction and synthetic boundaries; medium for the proposed measurable load limits because the intake does not set thresholds.

specialistReports.conclusion: Six-section single-page synthetic scope is sufficiently bounded. Fictional entries/placeholders are required content, not missing real assets. Adopt responsive/link/accessibility/source checks; numeric load targets remain optional and unapproved.

@make-proposal-agent rt-task-39d913b9-f059-48b7-b3a8-d5f9a6722164-RISK — FINAL INDEPENDENT CHALLENGE REPORT
Binding reviewed: project 804019a2-0012-4f8d-964e-1caa343e82a4; job e8c2e4a1-1546-45b3-b9f2-80b05000ecca; correlation discord-e8c2e4a1-1546-45b3-b9f2-80b05000ecca; intake revision 1. Analysis only: no approval, execution, deployment, commitment, reservation, spending or record change occurred.

A. Executive Assessment
The brief is a bounded synthetic, single responsive six-section website—not six separately routable pages—with three explicitly fictional portfolio examples and image placeholders. Its essential build scope is sufficiently stated for a planning baseline, but acceptance still needs decisions on the mailto recipient/default, placeholder format, source-handover format and the test interpretation of “accessible” and “reasonable load.” No deadline is agreed; therefore no delivery date can be promised. The 180,000-USD-cent value is a proposed estimate only, not agreed/received revenue, funding or a budget; no ledger data or financial model was available when this report was completed.

B. Scope and Requirements Challenges
Verified scope from the intake:
• Six sections: Home, About, Services, Portfolio, Our Process, Contact.
• Four titled/described service cards; three fictional portfolio entries with title, short description and image placeholder; five process stages.
• Responsive desktop/tablet/mobile frontend, section navigation, email link, consistent visual system, source code and basic deployment instructions.
• Acceptance: six sections work across target layout classes, navigation/contact links work, no major visual/functional defects.
• No CMS, contact form/email notification, SEO campaign, project-detail pages or public deployment is requested.

Challenge findings:
1. Do not convert “six sections” into six pages/routes. If a route-based architecture is proposed, it is a scope change requiring rationale and re-estimation.
2. “Functional email link” means a valid mailto: interaction, not confirmed email delivery, mailbox ownership or a contact form. The intended address is absent. A synthetic/reserved address is a proposed default only; a real address must be supplied before any real handover or deployment.
3. The fictional portfolio and image placeholders are required synthetic content, not missing client assets. Avoid external stock media, unlicensed imagery, invented client claims or fake performance results. Define whether placeholders are local CSS/SVG/labelled assets and how they are described to assistive technology.
4. “Optimized images and reasonable load” has no numeric threshold. It supports a bounded implementation/checklist—local lightweight placeholders, no unnecessary external media/scripts, responsive layout and recorded observations—but not a performance score, guaranteed metrics or SEO outcome.
5. “Modern, accessible frontend” requires a practical acceptance test (semantic landmarks/headings, keyboard navigation, visible focus, sensible link text, contrast/zoom smoke checks) but does not establish WCAG conformance/certification.
6. Source code and basic deployment instructions are deliverables even with no public deployment. They must specify prerequisite/runtime/build steps, configuration assumptions, static-host deployment example, and clearly state that no credentials/domain/provisioning/deployment was performed.

C. Delivery and Technical Feasibility
A limited static frontend is technically feasible in principle, conditioned on a bounded implementation: one page with in-page anchors; CSS/SVG or equivalent lightweight local placeholders; no CMS, form, API, analytics, external font/media dependency, real mail service or public launch. The realistic delivery duration cannot be stated as a commitment because capacity, environment, review cycle and chosen tooling are not given and the brief has no deadline. Any addition of real content, real mailbox, CMS, public host, SEO campaign, detail pages, external imagery/video or formal accessibility/performance target is a material revision requiring re-estimation.

D. Commitment and Effort Review
The brief expressly says no real client, payment or external commitment exists. That supports treating delivery labor and any template/font/image/hosting/vendor expense as unconfirmed planning exposure, not as liabilities. There is no evidence of a project ledger, resource booking, prior work, vendor license, source repository or deployment target. I requested Treasury’s task-specific bottom-up model directly in sw_b7c1b11860a749218497a95b7d17cc0e; no model was available at this report’s completion. A targeted reconciliation is required only if/when Treasury provides it.

E. Financial Review
Inputs supported by intake: proposedRevenueCents = 180,000 USD cents; agreedRevenueCents = null; received revenue = unverified/no evidence; delivery budget = not established.
Configured budget, confirmed commitments, settled spending, available funds, rate, contingency, external costs, overhead, tax and payment fees: unavailable.
Available funds cannot be calculated because no authoritative project ledger was supplied. Do not subtract potential template/font/hosting liabilities as confirmed commitments. Do not treat the proposed estimate as revenue, funding, authorization or a price ceiling.

F. Evidence and Verification
• Original dispatch/source binding: sw_c0b32f8f10bc694ff49ca20d06b285c4.
• Original intake attachment read directly: roomtreasury-intake.txt, mxc switch-media://77d910f3c62c44129636e9818d9899de.
• Challenge assignment and scope boundaries: sw_4a2ab48544a04bfab12b56b194558c0e.
• Treasury-model request: sw_b7c1b11860a749218497a95b7d17cc0e.
The supplied SHA-256 is preserved as intake metadata only. Canonical hashing inputs were not specified, so no cryptographic verification is claimed. No authoritative backend, contract, financial record, policy record, recipient/requester eligibility record, duplicate record or deployment evidence was accessed.

G. Risk Register
R1 | Scope architecture | High | Medium | Treating six sections as pages/routes increases navigation, QA and handover beyond the brief. | Preserve single-section architecture unless a revision is approved. | Research + Development.
R2 | Synthetic-content integrity | High | Medium | External/real media or invented claims can introduce rights, privacy or misleading-content exposure. | Use clearly labelled local placeholders and fictional descriptions only; no external assets without evidence. | Design + Development.
R3 | Mailto ambiguity | High | High | Missing target address prevents meaningful link acceptance; mailto does not prove delivery. | Obtain intended address or document synthetic default; test scheme/anchor behavior only. | Development + QA.
R4 | Accessibility ambiguity | High | Medium | “Accessible” can be mistaken for certification, creating acceptance disputes. | Apply and document semantic, keyboard/focus, contrast/zoom and link-text smoke checks; state no certification. | QA.
R5 | Performance ambiguity | Medium | High | “Reasonable load” can expand into unbounded optimization or score guarantees. | Keep local placeholders/light assets, avoid unnecessary dependencies, record representative observations; no threshold unless supplied. | Development + QA.
R6 | Navigation defects | Medium | Medium | In-page links can target incorrect/missing sections or become obscured by fixed headers. | Anchor-link/keyboard tests for all six destinations and target visibility. | Development + QA.
R7 | Source/handover gap | High | Medium | Code without usable instructions or dependency disclosure cannot be reproduced. | Include README, install/build/run/static-host steps, environment/dependency list and explicit no-deployment statement. | Development.
R8 | Schedule/capacity | High | Medium | No deadline, start trigger or resource assignment supports no delivery-date promise. | Supply only conditional duration after toolchain/capacity/review assumptions are agreed. | Research.
R9 | Hidden liabilities | Medium | Medium | Fonts/templates/hosting/deployment tooling may appear free but carry licence, renewal or configuration costs. | Use documented permissive/local assets where possible; identify unpriced external choices separately. | Research + Treasury.
R10 | Financial interpretation | Critical | High | Treating $1,800 proposed estimate as revenue/funds can cause unauthorized loss-making work. | Keep agreedRevenueCents null; obtain Treasury model and owner/ledger evidence before financial review. | Treasury + Owner.

H. Dependencies and Required Actions
1. Coordinator/Requirements: confirm the synthetic mailto address/default, placeholder convention, source-delivery format, and proposed smoke-test matrix.
2. Development: preserve a static single-page implementation; create local labelled placeholders; provide source and no-deploy deployment instructions.
3. QA: verify six section links, mailto scheme, responsive desktop/tablet/mobile layouts, keyboard/focus, visible focus/contrast/zoom smoke checks, no major defects and local-asset/load observations.
4. Treasury: provide task-specific cost/rate/contingency/margin model; challenge it against this bounded scope and assess any external-cost assumptions.
5. Commitment Intelligence/Owner: confirm no actual resource/vendor/ledger record is being treated as evidenced; retain unknowns as leads only.

I. Unresolved Questions
• What mailto address and contact information are intended for the synthetic contact section?
• Are image placeholders local SVG/CSS assets, or is a specific placeholder system requested?
• What source package/repository/archive and basic deployment-instruction format are expected?
• Which frontend toolchain/browser support set is assumed?
• Is any actual deployment, custom domain, real mail service, CMS, analytics, formal accessibility target or performance threshold later desired? None is currently included.
• What staffed capacity and review time support an estimated duration?
• What treasury model and external-cost/rate assumptions apply?

J. Cross-Agent Disagreements / Revision Comparison
No prior version or revised scope was supplied, so revision comparison is not applicable. No task-specific specialist conclusions were available at report completion. The material tension is not a disagreement: the scope is intentionally synthetic/static, while source/handover and mailto/QA obligations still need bounded interpretation.

K. Final Recommendation
NEEDS_MORE_INFORMATION for delivery planning and financial viability; the build scope may proceed only as a bounded synthetic planning baseline, not as approved execution. Before any owner review or action, resolve the mailto/source/acceptance decisions, obtain the Treasury model, confirm resources and preserve proposed revenue as non-revenue. No public deployment, payment, commitment or financial authorization is supported.

L. Confidence
High in the scope/evidence interpretation because the original attachment was read and expressly identifies a synthetic no-deployment/no-commitment project. Medium in technical risk assessment because no toolchain or handover target is stated. Low in cost, margin, available funds and capacity conclusions because no authoritative financial or staffing evidence exists.

followupResponses.reportText:
@treasury-ops-agent @make-proposal-agent rt-task-39d913b9-f059-48b7-b3a8-d5f9a6722164 — TARGETED FINANCIAL/SCOPE RECONCILIATION ADDENDUM (not a replacement final report)

Evidence reviewed: Treasury model sw_d9e35c79b4ba43518daccfe10087c855; intake/assignment sw_c0b32f8f10bc694ff49ca20d06b285c4 and sw_4a2ab48544a04bfab12b56b194558c0e.

Arithmetic check: correct.
• Planning hours: 4 + 7 + 15 + 6 = 32h.
• Base: 11,200 + 19,600 + 42,000 + 16,800 = 89,600 cents.
• Separate 20% contingency: 17,920 cents; total 107,520 cents.
• Low/high: 25h × 2,800 × 1.20 = 84,000; 39h × 2,800 × 1.20 = 131,040.
• Hypothetical margin against proposedRevenueCents 180,000 only: +96,000 (53.33%), +72,480 (40.27%), +48,960 (27.20%). agreedRevenueCents must remain null. These are not actual margins, available funds or authorization.

Scope/QA challenge
The 32h model is conditionally credible only for the stated single static six-section synthetic frontend. The model must retain these routine tasks inside base hours—not contingency:
1. Drafting and visibly labelling synthetic copy/three fictional portfolio entries and local image placeholders; no external/real client material.
2. Six in-page anchor-link tests, including keyboard activation and target visibility; no route/page expansion.
3. A valid mailto: scheme/link test. It does not demonstrate mail delivery; an absent recipient must be documented as a synthetic/clarification default rather than invented as a real mailbox.
4. Accessible-frontend smoke checks: semantic landmarks/headings, focus visibility, keyboard navigation, link text, contrast/zoom. This is not a certification.
5. Local/light asset and no-unnecessary-dependency checks plus recorded representative load observations. “Reasonable load” carries no score/threshold.
6. Source package/README with build/run/static-host guidance, dependencies and explicit statement that no public deployment, credentials, DNS or domain configuration occurred.

If the six QA/handover hours include those bounded checks, source packaging, one internal correction cycle and handover, I see no numerical correction. Any addition—real contact data/mail service, CMS, separate pages/detail pages, public deployment, external asset licensing, formal accessibility/performance certification, SEO campaign or additional review cycles—requires re-estimation and must not be concealed in the 17,920-cent contingency.

Schedule challenge
Eight to ten business days is a defensible conditional internal planning duration, not a promised deadline. It needs a start trigger, one scheduled designer/developer through the stated phases, ready internal review and no scope additions.
